name: T.J. Ricci
notes: Keeping this record. His middle name, Jeffrey, is for a cousin on his father's side.

name: Anna Marie Ricci
notes: Named for her great-grandmother on the Ricci side.

name: Jazlyn Morkert
notes: DeAnn's daughter, so T.J.'s half-sister on his mother's side. Named as one of Joe Morkert's nieces in 2003. Her father is not recorded here.

name: DeAnn Adel Morkert
notes: Her middle name, Adel, is for her grandmother Blanche Adele. She grew up around Scandia and Forest Lake.

name: Rodney Leo Morkert
notes: Named as a son in his father's 2011 obituary, and as the father on all three of his children's birth records. His middle name, Leo, is his father's.

name: Susan Marie (Houle) Morkert
notes: Born 10 February 1949 and appears as a one year old in the 1950 census at Forest Lake Township. Named as a daughter-in-law in Orris Morkert's obituary.

name: Kenneth Leo Morkert
notes: Lives in the Scandia and Forest Lake area.

name: Rebecca Morkert
notes: Kenneth's wife.

name: Olivia Morkert
notes: Kenneth and Rebecca's daughter. She is one of the four nieces and nephews named in Joe Morkert's 2003 obituary, alongside T.J., Anna and Jazlyn.

name: Joseph Robert "Joe" Morkert
notes: DeAnn's younger brother. He died at 27, living in Fridley and formerly of Scandia. The funeral was at St. Peter's Catholic Church in Forest Lake.

name: Orris Leo "Porky" Morkert
notes: Born on a farm at Leeds in North Dakota and known all his life as Porky. He registered for the draft at Leeds in June 1942, and moved to Minnesota after the war, settling around Forest Lake. His obituary names four children: Katherine Swingle, Rodney, Paulette Paumen and Richard.

name: Evelyn Anetta (Gunderson) Morkert
notes: Born at Harlow in Benson County, twenty miles from Leeds, so she and Orris were both North Dakota farm children from the same county. Her Social Security file names her parents as Anton and Inga Gunderson, which puts a Norwegian line into a family that is otherwise German and French-Canadian. She is buried at Scandinavian Cemetery in Forest Lake.

name: Archibald Monroe "Archie" Morkert
notes: Born in Indiana, a young single man in Alabama in 1910, and a farmer at Leeds in North Dakota from at least 1917 until 1950. He carried the family through three states in one lifetime.

name: Julia B. (Larson) Morkert
notes: Born in North Dakota, which makes her the first person on this branch not born east of the Mississippi. She was still at Leeds with Archibald in the 1950 census. Her maiden name, Larson, comes from her Find a Grave memorial rather than from a register, so it is a strong lead rather than a proof. Her memorial also puts her burial at Woodbine, Jo Daviess County, Illinois and her death in Washington state, neither of which is explained by anything else found so far.

name: Henry Newton Morkert
notes: A farmer at 28 in Carroll County, Indiana in 1880, in Baldwin County, Alabama by 1910, and in Benson County, North Dakota by 1930. His census entry in 1880 gives both of his own parents as born in Ohio, which is what points to Elias and Elizabeth.

name: Mary M. Morkert
notes: Born in Ohio and with Henry in Indiana, Alabama and North Dakota. Her maiden name is probably Thompson: a daughter's 1959 death record in Montana names her parents as Henry Morkert and Mary Thompson. One record is not proof.

name: Joseph C. Morkert
notes: Archie's older brother, two years old in the 1880 census. He went to North Dakota too, and earlier research has him prominent in Leeds.

name: Elias Silas Morkert
notes: Born in Ohio and farming in Clay Township, Carroll County, Indiana by 1880, two households from Henry. The link to Henry is not proven: it rests on the same township, the same surname, the right ages and the Ohio birthplaces that Henry's own census entry gives for his parents. What would settle it is Henry in this household in the 1860 or 1870 census, or Henry's 1933 death record. A Jno L. Morkert heads a household at Gratis in Preble County, Ohio in the 1820 census, the year before Elias was born in Ohio, which is the likeliest place this family was living then.

name: Elizabeth (Burkhalter) Morkert
notes: Born in Ohio to parents born in Pennsylvania. The surname comes from FamilySearch's own linking of this census entry to an Indiana marriage record, so it is a lead rather than a reading of the register itself. Burkhalter is Swiss German.

name: Lloyd Harry Houle
notes: He lived to 98 and spent nearly all of it in Forest Lake. He is buried at Calvary Cemetery there, although one index mis-maps the burial to a Calvary Cemetery in Washington County, Pennsylvania.

name: Blanche Adele (LaCasse) Houle
notes: Grew up in Centerville and married at Anoka in 1941. Her granddaughter DeAnn carries her middle name.

name: Cyrille Lacasse
notes: Head of a Lacasse household in Centerville, Anoka County in both 1920 and 1930, written Cyrille in one census and Cyril in the other. Earlier research gives him the middle name Joseph and a birth at Centerville in 1888, neither yet verified here.

name: Delina Lacasse
notes: Named in the same two censuses. Earlier research gives her maiden name as LaMotte, which is not proven.

name: John Joseph Houle

death.place: Forest Lake Township, Washington County, Minnesota

notes: He is the correction at the heart of this site. Earlier research had Lloyd's father as a David Houle born at Fort Ripley. The 1930 census and his own death record say otherwise: Lloyd was his son, and his own parents were John A. Houle and Mathilda Letourneau.

name: Lydia B. (Bernier) Houle
notes: She married at eighteen and appears with the family in the 1930 and 1940 censuses. Bernier is a surname new to this tree.

name: John A. Houle

death.place: Forest Lake Township, Washington County, Minnesota

notes: The first of this line born in America. The 1900 census narrows his birth to November 1868 and says he married in 1889; by 1910 he and Mathilda were at Columbus, a few miles from Centerville. He is six years old in the 1875 household with his father, mother and grandfather. His brothers there are Philias, Theodore, Thomas and William, and the eldest, Philias, was born in Michigan.

name: Mathilda (Letourneau) Houle
notes: Married John A. Houle in 1889 and appears with him and the children in the 1900 and 1910 censuses. Her surname comes from her son's death record. No birth year, no parents, and no record of her own has been found yet.

name: John Baptiste Houle
notes: His full name was John Baptiste, and his memorial gives an exact birth of 22 August 1842. He was brought from Quebec as a boy and died at Centerville eighty-six years later, buried at Saint Genevieve with his father. The 1900 census says he had been married thirty-three years, which puts the wedding at about 1867, and gives both of his own parents as born in French Canada.

name: Virginia (Tourville) Houle
notes: Twenty-eight in 1875 and fifty-three in 1900, born in French Canada both times, so she came from Quebec rather than being born here. She and John Baptiste were married about 1867 and had at least eight children. A Euphemie Tourville, fourteen and also Quebec-born, is in the household in 1875, most likely her sister.

name: Michel "Michael" Houle
notes: Now dated, not just named. He is at Centerville in the 1875 state census aged 70 and again in 1895 aged about 89, and his memorial gives 29 September 1802 to 6 December 1898, buried at Saint Genevieve Cemetery. He was ninety-six. Earlier research guessed 1806 and 1898 for him; the death is exact and the birth is four years out. One warning about the memorial: the index maps Saint Genevieve Cemetery to Shoreham, Vermont. It is Centerville, Minnesota. A Zotique Houle appears in the same Vermont-labelled cemetery and in the Minnesota county death register on the same day in 1897, which is what gives the error away.

name: Thomas Houle
notes: John B.'s younger brother, and the reason Michel can be named at all. His death record gives their father as Mitchell Houle and his own mother as Kadzi Tougon, which is a clerk's rendering of a French name, most likely Tougas. A different mother from John B. would mean two marriages.

name: Anton Gunderson
notes: Named on his daughter's Social Security file. The family was at Harlow in Benson County, North Dakota, where Evelyn was born in 1922. Gunderson is Norwegian, and nothing else about him has been found yet.

name: Inga Gunderson
notes: Named on her daughter's Social Security file, with no surname given other than her married one. Inga is a Norwegian name, as is Anton.

name: John L. Morkert
notes: Head of a household at Gratis, Preble County, Ohio in the 1820 census, the year before Elias Morkert was born in Ohio. An 1820 census names only the head, so this is a name and a place and nothing more. Earlier research named a John Lewis Morkert as an early American ancestor and put him in Indiana. The name turns out to be real and the place turns out to be Ohio. Whether he is Elias's father is not proven.

name: Dylan Morkert
notes: Kenneth and Rebecca's son. He is not among the four nieces and nephews listed in the 2003 obituary, so he was most likely born after it.
